info.title: Tenor API
info.summary: Quotes and ready-to-sign payloads for lending and borrowing on Tenor, at a fixed or a variable rate. Tenor never signs, sends or holds a key: your wallet signs and sends every payload.
info.description:
Lend and borrow on Tenor, at a fixed or a variable rate, using your non-custodial wallet of choice. Tenor never signs, sends or holds a key.

1. **Find a market.** `GET /v1/markets` returns every market with its open maturities.
2. **Quote.** `POST /v1/quotes` gives the rate for a size right now.
3. **Prepare.** `POST /v1/lend/prepare`, or the prepare of any other action, returns the transactions to sign, already simulated and checked.
4. **Sign and send** the transactions from your wallet.
5. **Track.** `GET /v1/transactions/{tx_hash}` reports when the transaction is included in a block and what it filled.

Reads and quotes are public. Prepares need an API key.

## Conventions

| Convention | Rule | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Amounts | Integer strings in the token's smallest unit, never rounded | `"1000000"` = 1 USDC |
| Rates | Annual rate (APR) as a decimal string, in fields ending in `_rate` | `"0.052"` = 5.2% |
| Times | Unix seconds. A field ending in `_at` is a moment, and one ending in `_s` is a duration. `meta.generated_at` is the only ISO 8601 timestamp | `matures_at`, `time_to_maturity_s` |
| Chains | `chain_id` on every chain-scoped request: in the query on GET, in the body on POST | `chain_id=8453` |
| IDs | Opaque strings, unique within a chain | `maturity_id` |
| Addresses | Accepted in any case, returned checksummed | `0x833589fCD6…` |
| Paging | Offers, positions and fills are paged with `cursor` and `limit` (default 50, max 200). `meta.next_cursor` is `null` on the last page. Catalog lists (chains, tokens, markets, maturities, curves, balances) are short and aren't paged | `limit=50` |
| Options | Opt-in flags start with `include_` | `include_onchain=true` |
| Client IDs | A `client_id` passed on a prepare is echoed back and logged | |
| Compatibility | Fields, enum values and error codes are only ever added. Ignore unknown fields, and handle unknown values | |

## Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| market | A loan token and the collateral tokens borrowers can post for it. A market groups every maturity of the pair and its variable rate |
| maturity | One fixed term of a market, at fixed rates, ending at `matures_at` |
| variable rate | A market's floating rate, with no term. Lent and borrowed under `/v1/variable/*`, by `market_id` |
| deprecated | A market or maturity that Tenor is phasing out. Tenor no longer lists it and its liquidity runs off, but it still trades |
| best rate / mid rate | The best lend or borrow rate available now, and the midpoint between the two |
| term structure | The best rates on every maturity of a market, side by side |
| market depth | The open offers on a maturity, grouped by rate |
| liquidity | The amount that can be lent or borrowed at the current rates |
| settlement fee / continuous fee | A fee taken from each fill, and a fee that accrues on a lend until maturity |
| principal | The amount that changes hands now |
| amount at maturity | The amount owed, or paid back, at maturity |
| quote | The rate for a size right now. A quote is a preview and commits to nothing |
| offer | A firm commitment to lend or borrow at a rate, open until it fills, expires or is cancelled |
| ladder | Several offers posted together at stepped rates or sizes |
| staircase | Offers posted together in back-to-back time windows, so that together they hold one rate as maturity nears. Listed as one entry |
| group / OCO | Offers that share their fills. Cancelling a group cancels all of its offers. With `oco` (one cancels the other), a ladder shares one group, so a fill on one offer reduces the others |
| idle capital | The capital behind a lend offer, earning the variable rate until a taker fills the offer |
| lending vault | The contract that holds a market's variable lends, idle capital included (`onchain.lending_vault` in `GET /v1/markets`) |
| deposit on fill | A borrow offer whose collateral stays in the wallet until the offer fills |
| passive quoting curve | A maker's lend and exit rates by time to maturity, quoted on every maturity of a market |
| exit rate | The rate at which a curve resells the maker's fixed lends (`resell_rate`) |
| position | A fixed or variable lend or borrow held by a wallet |
| LLTV / LTV | The loan-to-value at which a borrow can be liquidated, and the borrow's current loan-to-value |
| liquidation price | The collateral price at which a borrow becomes liquidatable |
| cost basis / P&L | The cost of opening a position, and its profit or loss since |

| Action | Description |
| --- | --- |
| lend / borrow | Open or add to a fixed-rate position on a maturity |
| repay | Pay back a borrow, early by taking offers or in full |
| resell | Exit a lend before maturity by reselling it to another lender |
| redeem | Collect a lend from what borrowers have repaid, usually at maturity |
| take | Accept one specific offer |
| manage | Add or withdraw collateral, or set auto-renewal, without changing the debt |
| renew | Roll a position into a later maturity of the same market |
| migrate | Move a variable borrow to a fixed rate |
| post / cancel | Post offers, or cancel them |
| clear | Stop a curve from quoting |

## Authentication

- Reads and quotes are public. Prepares, simulations, readiness and `GET /v1/access` need an API key in the `X-Api-Key` header.
- A key carries scopes: `read` for keyed reads and `trade` to prepare payloads. Each route states the scope it needs.
- Keys starting with `tnr_sk_test_` are test keys. They work like live keys, but every prepare is a dry run.
- A key sent on a public route identifies the caller. An invalid key is rejected there too.
- `GET /v1/access` checks a key. A revoked key stops working within 30 seconds.
- Keep keys on your servers. Never ship a key to a browser or an app.

## Payloads

Every `POST …/prepare` returns a payload for one wallet: the transactions to sign, a one-line `summary`, and a `preview` of their effects.

Declare how the wallet signs in `wallet_kind`, and the payload is built for that wallet. If the wallet's code doesn't match, the payload carries a `WALLET_KIND_MISMATCH` warning. A smart account isn't deployed until its first operation, so `smart_account` is never flagged.

| `wallet_kind` | Send | Signing window |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `eoa` | Each of `steps` in order, waiting for each receipt; or `requires`, then `transaction` | 5 min |
| `delegated_eoa` (EIP-7702) | `calls` in one `wallet_sendCalls`, or as an `eoa` | 5 min |
| `safe` | `safe_tx` as one Safe transaction (MultiSendCallOnly, delegate call) | 30 min |
| `smart_account` | `calls` in one user operation | 30 min |

- **Checks.** Each payload is simulated as returned, from the wallet, at the latest block, and then checked: approvals match the size (except a curve's setup, which approves the vault's shares in full to the curve's callback, for every curve on that vault), the rate and the deadline are bounded onchain, and every call goes to Tenor's contracts. If a check fails, the prepare returns an error and no calldata.
- **Validity.** `limit_rate` and the deadline are enforced onchain. A payload included in a block after `validity.until_at` reverts, so it never fills at a worse rate. If you can't sign before `until_at` minus `validity.recommended_margin_s`, prepare again.
- **Approvals.** `requires` lists the approvals and the one-time authorization the wallet still needs, as of the prepare. Wait until each payload is included in a block before you prepare the next one.
- **Fresh quotes.** Each prepare quotes again and never reuses an earlier quote. `preview` is the result of the simulation: the size, the rate with fees, the offers filled and the wallet's balance changes.
- **No quote.** A payload that fills no offers (a redeem, a direct repay, a manage, a variable action) has no `quote` and no `limit_rate`. Its `bounds` and `validity.until_at` are `null`.
- **Dry run.** `dry_run: true` runs the same quote, simulation and checks, with the wallet funded in the simulation. It works for a wallet that holds nothing yet. The response has `status: preview_only`, the full `preview` and `requires`, and nothing to send. Test keys always dry run.
- **Sanctions.** Wallets on the OFAC sanctions list get `403 WALLET_BLOCKED`. The key that prepares doesn't matter.
- **Debugging.** `include_onchain: true` adds `onchain`: the payload's calls decoded by their ABIs, nested bundles included, with the result of each call in the simulation and the events it emitted. `onchain` follows the contracts' ABIs and changes with them, so the compatibility rule in Conventions doesn't cover it.

## Responses

- A success is `{ "data": …, "meta": { "request_id", "generated_at", … } }`.
- An error is `{ "error": { "code", "category", "treatment", "message", "details", "request_id" } }`.
- Branch on `code`. For an unknown code, act on `treatment`: `fix_request`, `refetch_state`, `fund_account` or `retry`.
- A payload can carry `warnings`, which never block it. Show the `message` of an unknown warning.
- Every response carries `X-Request-Id`. Send your own (up to 128 of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -`) to match our logs with yours.

## Rate limits

Each route counts against one of three budgets, so a burst of quotes can't block a cancel. With a key, budgets are per key. Without one, they are per IP address.

| Budget | Routes | With a key | Without |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `read` | Reads | 1200 / 60 s | 25 / 1 s, 150 / 10 s, 1000 / 60 s |
| `compute` | Quotes, takeable offers, simulations, readiness, prepares | 120 / 60 s | 30 / 60 s |
| `cancel` | Cancels and curve clears | 600 / 60 s | Key only |

- Treat limits as approximate: each server counts on its own, and requests are spread across servers.
- Every response carries `X-RateLimit-Policy`, `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`.
- Past a limit, requests get `429 RATE_LIMITED`, with `Retry-After` in seconds. Wait that long before retrying.
- After 30 failed key checks in a minute, an IP address gets `429` on every request that sends a key.

## Caching

- Slow-changing reads (catalog, market state, market depth) send `Cache-Control` with a `max-age`, and an `ETag`. Revalidate with `If-None-Match`: an unchanged response is a `304` with no body.
- Quotes, payloads and anything about one wallet are `no-store`. Don't cache them.
- A transaction is `no-store` until it is final and indexed. After that, it may be cached for a minute.
- `meta.generated_at` is when the data was read, which can be up to `max-age` ago.

## Live data

Market depth and quotes stream over a WebSocket at `wss://router.tenor.finance/socket` (Phoenix Channels), on the `orderbook:{maturity_id}` and `quotes:{maturity_id}` topics, updated every block. Use the stream to know when to quote again. Prepare through this API, which checks every payload before you sign it.

tags.name: Catalog
tags.description:
Chains, tokens, markets and maturities served by the API. The catalog carries no rates: rates come from quotes and market depth.

- `GET /v1/chains` lists the chains served, with `capabilities` (the features the API supports there) and `status`. Treat an unknown capability as off. While a chain is `degraded`, prepares fail with a `retry` treatment and reads keep working.
- `GET /v1/markets` returns each market with its open maturities, so one call is enough to start.
- `listing` tells two kinds of market apart. `listed` markets are curated by Tenor, on a regular maturity cadence. `otc` markets are any other market whose tokens are all whitelisted, whose oracles scale by its tokens' decimals, and that has no enter or liquidator gate. Lists return `listed` markets unless you pass `listing=otc` or `listing=all`. Curves, renews, migrations and auto-renewal only target `listed` markets.
- **Tenor doesn't review OTC markets.** Passing the checks above doesn't make one safe. Read its `collaterals[].oracle` and `lltv` before you lend or borrow on it.
- An ID that exists onchain but isn't served gets `422 MARKET_NOT_SUPPORTED`. Positions on maturities or markets that are no longer served can still be closed, unless the market uses a blocked token.
- Deprecated markets and maturities still trade while Tenor phases them out. Lists hide them unless you pass `include_deprecated=true`. A prepare that adds exposure to one carries a `MARKET_DEPRECATED` warning.

tags.name: Market depth
tags.description:
The open offers on each maturity, before fees. Every caller sees the same depth, refreshed once a block.

- `GET /v1/maturities/{maturity_id}/depth` groups the open offers into rate levels. Lenders post `lend_offers`, which you borrow from, and you lend into `borrow_offers`. Depth rates are the makers' rates, before fees: quote a size to get its rate.
- `GET /v1/maturities/{maturity_id}/takeable-offers` lists the offers that can be taken right now, with live amounts, for `POST /v1/take/prepare`.
- `GET /v1/markets/{market_id}/term-structure` lines up the best rates of every open maturity next to the market's variable rates.
- A maturity with withdrawable liquidity carries a 0% lend offer (`syn:withdrawable:<maturity_id>`, `kind: withdrawable`). It is real liquidity, so it can make the depth look crossed: `best_borrow_rate` is `0` and `spread` negative.

tags.name: Quotes
tags.description:
The rate for a size right now, with fees included. A quote is a preview and commits to nothing: each prepare quotes again and enforces its own limit rate onchain.

- `POST /v1/quotes` quotes one maturity. `POST /v1/quotes/term-structure` quotes the same size on every maturity of a market.
- Size a quote by `principal` (the amount that changes hands now) or by `amount_at_maturity`. The quote returns both.
- Pass the `wallet_kind` that will sign, so the quote fills like its prepare.
- When nothing can fill the size, the quote fails with a `422` and never returns a 0% rate. Set `allow_partial` to quote the part the open offers can fill.

tags.name: Fixed rate
tags.description:
Lend, borrow and exit on a maturity at a fixed rate.

**Lend and borrow.** Size by `principal` (the amount lent or received now) or by `amount_at_maturity` (the amount paid back or owed). A lend with `post_rest` fills the open offers at `limit_rate` or better and posts the rest as a lend offer, in the same payload. When no offer meets the limit, the payload only posts. A borrow can deposit collateral in the same payload with `deposit_collateral`.

**One side per maturity.** A wallet can't lend and borrow on the same maturity (`422 OPPOSITE_POSITION`). Resell or repay first.

**Exits.** Repay, resell and redeem close a position on its `maturity_id`. Leave `size` out to close the whole position. A wallet without the position gets `404 POSITION_NOT_FOUND`, which names the action that fits the position it holds.
- **Repay** pays a borrow back early by taking offers, or in full with `direct: true`. After maturity, every repay is direct.
- **Resell** exits a lend before maturity. **Redeem** collects it from what borrowers have repaid, usually after maturity.

**Take** accepts one offer by `offer_id`, with no fallback. `quote.action` says whether the take lends or borrows.

**Manage** moves collateral without changing the debt. **Renew** rolls a whole position into a later maturity of the same market, and **migrate** moves a variable borrow to a fixed rate. Both work now (`mode: spot`) or through an offer (`mode: limit`).

**Auto-renewal.** `renewal` on a borrow or a manage renews the market's borrows before they mature, and falls back to the variable rate when no renewal fills.

**Previews.** `preview.position_before` and `preview.position_after` show the position before and after the payload. A payload that leaves the position above 95% of its borrow capacity gets a `HEALTH_THRESHOLD` warning. Health never blocks a payload.

tags.name: Variable rate
tags.description:
Lend or borrow a market's loan token at its floating rate, with no term. These actions mirror the fixed ones, but take a `market_id` instead of a maturity. A market's variable rate is `variable` in `GET /v1/markets`.

- **Lend** deposits into the market's lending vault. The deposit earns the variable rate and funds the wallet's idle-capital offers and passive quoting curve on the market. **Withdraw** takes it back, up to the part variable borrowers haven't borrowed.
- **Borrow**, **repay** and **manage** work like their fixed counterparts, against the market's `variable.collateral_token`.
- A withdrawal that leaves the wallet's idle-capital offers or curves short gets an `IDLE_CAPITAL_SHORTFALL` or `CURVE_UNFUNDED` warning.
- `preview.variable_lend` and `preview.variable_borrow` show the position before and after the payload.

tags.name: Transactions
tags.description:
Simulate calls right before the wallet sends them, and track transactions after they are sent.

**Simulate.** `POST /v1/simulate` runs calls held before signing, or edited by a Safe or custodian, through the checks that don't need the original request. The response is always a 200, with a `status` of `ok`, `reverts` or `unsafe`. Calls to contracts outside Tenor's are simulated, but Tenor doesn't check what they do: check for a `FOREIGN_CALL` warning as well as `status`.

**Track.** Poll `GET /v1/transactions/{tx_hash}` until `status` is `confirmed` or `reverted`, which are final, and `indexed` is `true`. The transaction's fills, position changes and offer changes come from Tenor's records. Rarely, Tenor records an event after `indexed` is `true`, so reconcile fills from `/fills` (see Accounts).

tags.name: Accounts
tags.description:
Positions, fills and balances of a wallet on one chain.

- **Positions** lists fixed and variable lends and borrows. Amounts, collateral and health are read onchain. Cost basis and P&L come from Tenor's records of the wallet's fills. Positions in markets the catalog no longer lists are still returned.
- **Fills** lists every fill the wallet took part in, as maker or taker. Tenor can record a fill late, below a cursor you already hold. To read new fills, poll with `from_block` from a few blocks before the last fill you saw, and drop the `fill_id`s you already have.
- **Balances** lists the wallet's non-zero balances, read onchain, of the tokens of every market the API serves, listed and OTC, and of any token its offers reserve. `reserved` is the part its open offers can still take, and `available` the part it can move without leaving them short. Amounts inside Tenor are positions, not balances.

tags.name: Offers
tags.description:
Post firm offers, read them back with their live status, keep them fillable, and cancel them.

**Post.** `POST /v1/offers/post/prepare` posts one offer, or a ladder of offers at stepped rates or sizes, on one maturity or several. Each offer holds its `rate` onchain until it expires or its maturity, whichever comes first. With `oco: true`, the offers share one fill limit.
- Pass groups to `replace_groups` to cancel old offers in the same payload as the new ones. `cancels` in the response lists what they end. Groups aren't checked against Tenor's records, since one posted a moment ago may not be in them yet: a group with none of the wallet's live offers ends nothing, and gets a `NOTHING_TO_REPLACE` warning.
- A post can't cross the wallet's own open offers on the other side of a maturity (`422 SELF_CROSS`). An offer that holds a fixed discount instead of a rate is compared at its rate closest to the post's, since that rate climbs as maturity nears.
- A lend post prepares even when the wallet holds less than its offers can pull, on top of what its other open offers reserve, with an `OFFER_UNFUNDED` warning. Takers fill only the amount the wallet holds when they take.
- A borrow post prepares even when the collateral on a maturity can't back what its offers there can borrow, with a `COLLATERAL_SHORTFALL` warning. A fill past what the collateral carries fails: deposit collateral first, or post with `deposit_on_fill`.

**Idle capital.** `idle_capital: true` on a lend post keeps the budget lent at the variable rate until a taker fills, and pays each fill from that variable lend. All the maturities of one post must share a lending vault. A fill the variable lend can't pay out at that moment fails, and Tenor's quote engine skips the offer until it can. The post tops the variable lend up to the budget from the wallet, which must hold the difference (`422 INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`); a dry run funds it in the simulation instead.

**Deposit on fill.** `collateral.deposit_on_fill: true` on a borrow post leaves the collateral in the wallet until each offer fills, so a borrow ladder needs nothing up front. If the wallet holds less than the collateral, the payload carries a `COLLATERAL_UNFUNDED` warning.

**Read.** `GET /v1/offers?maker=` lists a wallet's offers with their live status. A staircase is listed as one entry. Offers on maturities the API doesn't serve are listed too, with `served: false`, since a cancel ends them. `GET /v1/offers/{offer_id}` reads one offer, including `syn:` offers quoted from a passive quoting curve. A new offer can read `invalid` (`RATIFIER_UNAUTHORIZED`) for about 20 s after its transaction is indexed, until Tenor's quote engine reads the wallet's authorization.

**Readiness.** An open offer fills later, with no prepare, and silently stops filling when the wallet falls short. `GET /v1/accounts/{wallet}/readiness` checks the authorizations, allowances and balances the wallet's offers need, and returns the transactions that fix what is `missing`. Prepares carry their own approvals, so a post doesn't need readiness first. Check again after moving funds or approving elsewhere.

**Cancel.** `POST /v1/offers/cancel/prepare` cancels by `offer_ids`, `groups`, `maturity_id`, `market_id` or `all`. IDs aren't checked against the catalog: one with none of the wallet's live offers, an unknown one included, gets `422 NOTHING_TO_CANCEL`. Cancelling every live offer of a group ends the whole group. Cancelling only some revokes the Merkle root they were signed under, which can end more offers (`CANCELS_MORE`). A large cancel can take several payloads (`MORE_TO_CANCEL`). Cancels keep working while quoting is down.

tags.name: Passive quoting
tags.description:
A passive quoting curve is one set of rates that quotes every maturity of a market, with no transaction per quote.

- A curve has 2 to 8 points of `{ time_to_maturity_s, lend_rate, resell_rate }`. The curve lends a vault's idle capital into each maturity at `lend_rate`, and resells the wallet's fixed lends at the exit rate, `resell_rate`, returning the capital to the vault.
- Tenor's quote engine turns the curve into offers and updates their rates about every block. A new curve, or one with new rates, starts quoting within a minute.
- `POST /v1/curves/set/prepare` sets a curve. The first set writes the curve's setup and funds its vault (`enable`). After that, a set that keeps the first and last points is one call (`reprice`).
- One vault can back curves on every market with the same loan token, so one deposit funds them all.
- Rates are stored per second, rounded in the maker's favour by under 3.2e-11 a year, and read back as set. The live offers sit on the market's tick grid, up to one tick step in the maker's favour, so a take rate can differ a little from `GET /v1/curves/preview`.
- Every set is written, even one identical to the stored curve.
- Curves renew on the last-Friday-of-month cadence. The API takes no cadence, and every set that writes the setup writes that cadence again.
- `POST /v1/curves/clear/prepare` stops a curve from quoting and keeps its setup. `GET /v1/curves/preview` shows a curve's quotes on every maturity now.

post.description:
Sets the wallet's passive quoting curve on a market. The curve's `points` quote every maturity of the market, with no transaction per quote. When the setup is in place and the first and last points don't move, the payload is one call that only updates the rates (`curve.mode: reprice`). A set identical to the stored curve is still written.

Otherwise (`enable`), the payload also writes the curve's setup: the authorizations, the lend and exit setup, and an approval of all the vault's shares to the curve's callback. Every curve on the vault shares that approval, the one approval the API makes for more than the payload moves. `fund` deposits idle capital into the curve's vault in the same payload. The setup always writes the last-Friday-of-month renewal cadence. The API takes no cadence, and every `enable` writes that cadence again. Without idle capital, the curve quotes nothing, and the payload carries a `CURVE_UNFUNDED` warning.

Needs an API key with the `trade` scope.

post.description:
Cancels the wallet's offers. Pass exactly one of `offer_ids`, `groups`, `maturity_id`, `market_id`, or `all: true` for every offer on the chain. Cancels count against the `cancel` budget, apart from quotes and prepares.

When every live offer of a group is cancelled, the whole group ends, and none of its offers can be taken again. Cancelling only some of a group's offers, such as one offer of an `oco` group, revokes the Merkle root they were signed under. Any other offer signed under that root ends too: `cancels.offer_ids` lists it, and a `CANCELS_MORE` warning names it. One payload ends at most 256 groups and roots. Past that, a `MORE_TO_CANCEL` warning gives the number left, to cancel once this payload is included in a block.

Needs an API key with the `trade` scope.

post.description:
Rolls the wallet's whole position on `maturity_id` into `target_maturity_id`, a later maturity of the same market. A borrow moves its debt and collateral, and a lend its amount at maturity. Tenor reads the side onchain.

In `spot` mode, the payload renews now, bounded onchain on the target by `limit_rate` and `deadline_at`. A borrow first repays its debt early by taking offers, for less than the amount owed where offers allow (`preview.source.bought_back`), and repays the rest in full. A lend renews from the amount borrowers have repaid into its maturity, so usually after the maturity. In `limit` mode, the payload posts an offer at `limit_rate` until `expires_at` (`offers`). Each fill rolls its share of the position.

`preview.source` is the position the payload closes, and the rest of `preview` is the target. To renew automatically, set `renewal` on `/v1/borrow/prepare` or `/v1/manage/prepare`.

Needs an API key with the `trade` scope.

Each group counts once, at its largest unfilled offer. Scheduled offers and offers that can't be taken now count too, since funding the wallet makes them fillable again. vault.description: The vault the curve's lend and exit setup uses, which `disable` removes. Defaults to it. A named vault must be listed for the market's loan token and be the one the wallet's setup on the market uses (`422 VAULT_NOT_SUPPORTED`).

disable.description: Also remove the lend and exit setup. Without `disable`, only the curve is cleared, and the next `POST /v1/curves/set/prepare` sets the curve in one call.

delta.description: The change in collateral posted. Signed integer string in the token's smallest unit, negative for a decrease.

status.description: `active`: the curve quotes every maturity in its window. `paused`: Tenor has halted curve quoting, so no curve quotes until quoting resumes. `missing_authorization`: the wallet revoked the curve's authorization, or the allowance its fills use. `missing_params`: the lend and exit setup is gone. `cleared`: cleared, with its last points kept. When several apply, the first of `cleared`, `missing_params`, `missing_authorization` and `paused` wins. `POST /v1/curves/set/prepare` fixes all but `paused`.

points.description: 1 to 8 points in ascending time to maturity. The curve's rate at any time to maturity is the straight line between the two nearest points, and the end point's rate past either end. Rates are stored onchain per second, `lend_rate` rounded up and `resell_rate` down by under 3.2e-11 a year. They read back rounded to 10 decimals, which gives the rates as set.

window.description: The maturities the curve lends into, by time to maturity: its first and last points when it was set. `null` while the curve has no lend and exit setup.

mode.description: `clear`: removes only the curve, so nothing is quoted. `disable`: removes the curve and its lend and exit setup.

status.description: `quoted`: Tenor holds a takeable offer that lends from the vault on this maturity.

anyOf.description: The principal a borrower can take now: the idle capital, minus the fee and the part the lending vault can't pay out. `null` when not quoted. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

reason.description: Why this side isn't quoted, or why it quotes less than it could. New codes can be added. Codes include `OUTSIDE_WINDOW` (the maturity is outside the curve's window), `UNFUNDED` (no idle capital), `NO_VAULT_LIQUIDITY` (the vault can't pay out the wallet's shares now, because its markets are lent out), `MISSING_AUTHORIZATION`, `MISSING_APPROVAL`, `MISSING_PARAMS`, `POLICY_PAUSED`, `CURVE_CLEARED`, `PENDING` (Tenor can't tell yet), `NOT_QUOTED` (no offer yet; Tenor reads a new curve within a minute) and `UNAVAILABLE` (nothing is quoted, and Tenor's quote engine gives no reason). `null` when nothing limits the quote.

anyOf.description: The curve's lend rate on this maturity at `meta.block_number`, before fees. `null` when the curve holds no points. The live offer is priced on the market's tick grid, rounded in the maker's favour by up to one tick step, and its take rate also counts the continuous fee. Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).
The curve's exit rate on this maturity at `meta.block_number`, before fees. `null` when the curve holds no points. Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).

resell.description: `null` unless Tenor holds an offer reselling the wallet's lend on this maturity.

lend_rate.description: The rate the curve lends at on this maturity now, before fees. Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).

resell_rate.description: The curve's exit rate on this maturity now, before fees. Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).

in_window.description: Whether the maturity is inside the curve's window, so the curve lends into it.

policy.description: The contract that holds the curve's points.

vault.description: The vault the curve lends from and returns exit proceeds to: the vault its setup uses, or else the market's lending vault.

time_to_maturity_s.description: The time to maturity this point applies to, in seconds.

lend_rate.description: The rate the maker lends at on a maturity this far from maturing: the rate a borrower gets. Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).

resell_rate.description: The exit rate: the rate the maker resells its fixed lends at on a maturity this far from maturing. Below `lend_rate`. Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).

authorized.description: Whether the wallet has authorized the contract that validates the curve's offers.

approved.description: Whether the wallet has approved the curve's vault shares, for at least its share balance, to the contract that pulls the shares on each fill.

idle_capital.description: The idle capital the wallet holds in the curve's vault, which the curve's fills lend from. Every curve on that vault uses this same balance. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

status.description: `quoted`: Tenor holds a takeable offer that resells the wallet's lend on this maturity.

anyOf.description: The amount the wallet's lend on this maturity resells for now. `null` when not quoted. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

rate.description: The level's rate, rounded toward zero to `bucket_bps`. Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).

liquidity.description: The principal available at this level. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

cumulative_liquidity.description: The principal from the best level through this one. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

code.description: Stable error code to branch on. New codes may be added; handle unknown ones by `treatment`.

treatment.description: The next step: fix the request, refetch state, fund the account, or retry.

message.description: A readable explanation. For a validation error, the first problem. Don't parse the message.

details.description: Context for the code. side.description: Whether the wallet lent or borrowed in this fill.

role.description: `maker`: one of the wallet's offers was taken. `taker`: the wallet took an offer.

group.description: The `group` of the maker's offer that filled, the same value as on the offer. `null` on an older fill until Tenor records it.

anyOf.description: The settlement fee the lender paid on top of the amount the borrower received. `null` when Tenor can't determine the fee. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

amount_at_maturity.description: The amount the fill adds to the amount owed at maturity. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

registry.description: One check per enabled chain, keyed by chain ID: whether the SDK's contract registry and the indexer agree.

Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).

renewal.description: Change the market's auto-renewal, on its own or with a collateral change. Turning auto-renewal on needs a borrow on this maturity.

market_id.description: The market's ID, unique per chain.

listing.description: `listed`: a market Tenor curates, on a regular maturity cadence. `otc`: any other market whose loan token and collateral tokens are all whitelisted, whose oracles scale by its tokens' decimals, and that has no enter or liquidator gate. An OTC market's maturities are the ones offers name. Tenor doesn't review OTC markets: check their oracles and LLTVs before trading.

structure.description: The collateral a borrower can post. `plain`: the collateral token. `loan_token`: the collateral token, or the loan token itself. `yield`: the collateral token, or `yield_shares` that earn this market's variable rate, so posted collateral keeps earning.

lltv.description: The LLTV: the loan-to-value at which a borrow against this collateral can be liquidated. Decimal fraction string ("0.86" = 86%).

oracle.description: The price oracle for this collateral.

liquidation_cursor.description: The liquidation cursor of Morpho Midnight, the Morpho fixed-rate protocol Tenor is built on. It sets the liquidation incentive from the LLTV. Decimal fraction string ("0.86" = 86%).

collaterals.description: Every token a borrower can post.

variable_market_id.description: The variable market behind this market's variable rate.

collateral_token.description: The only token a variable borrow can post as collateral.

lltv.description: The variable borrow's LLTV. Decimal fraction string ("0.86" = 86%).

irm.description: The interest rate model of the Morpho variable rate.

variable.description: The market's variable rate. `null` when it has none.

maturities.description: Maturities open for new lends and borrows, earliest first. Deprecated maturities are listed only with `include_deprecated`.

total_borrowed.description: Principal borrowed across every maturity. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

tags.description: Labels for grouping, such as `STABLE` or `BTC`.

deprecated_at.description: When the market or maturity was deprecated, in Unix seconds. `null` when it isn't deprecated. Tenor is phasing out a deprecated market or maturity: Tenor no longer lists it, and its liquidity runs off. It still trades, and a prepare that adds exposure to it carries a `MARKET_DEPRECATED` warning.

rcf_threshold.description: Midnight's recovery close factor floor: a liquidation that would leave collateral worth less than this amount may take the whole position. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

enter_gate.description: Midnight's enter gate. The zero address when there is none.

liquidator_gate.description: Midnight's liquidator gate. The zero address when there is none.

anyOf.description: The lending vault that holds variable lends and idle capital. `null` when there is none.

lend_offers.description: Levels of offers made by lenders, which a caller borrows from, lowest rate first.

borrow_offers.description: Levels of offers made by borrowers, which a caller lends into, highest rate first.

anyOf.description: The lowest rate in `lend_offers`: the rate borrowing pays now. `null` when there are no lend offers. A maturity with withdrawable liquidity carries a 0% lend offer (`syn:withdrawable:<maturity_id>`), so this can be `0`. Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).
The highest rate in `borrow_offers`: the rate lending earns now. `null` when there are no borrow offers. Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).
Halfway between the two best rates. `null` unless both sides have offers. Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).

`best_borrow_rate` minus `best_lend_rate`. `null` unless both sides have offers. Negative when the 0% withdrawable offer sits below the best borrow offer. Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).

variable.description: The market's variable rates. `null` when the market has no variable rate.

maturities.description: Every maturity not yet matured, earliest first.

maturity_id.description: The maturity's ID, unique per chain.

matures_at.description: When positions in this maturity come due, in Unix seconds.

deprecated_at.description: When the market or maturity was deprecated, in Unix seconds. `null` when it isn't deprecated. Tenor is phasing out a deprecated market or maturity: Tenor no longer lists it, and its liquidity runs off. It still trades, and a prepare that adds exposure to it carries a `MARKET_DEPRECATED` warning.

settlement_fee_rate.description: The settlement fee a fill pays right now, as a share of its principal. Not annualized, and it depends on the time to maturity. Decimal fraction string ("0.86" = 86%).

continuous_fee_rate.description: The continuous fee, as an annual rate taken from the amount lenders are owed at maturity. Decimal fraction string ("0.86" = 86%).

total_borrowed.description: Total principal borrowed on this maturity. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

total_amount_at_maturity.description: The total amount lenders are owed at maturity. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

total_bad_debt.description: Debt left unpaid after liquidations. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

state.description: Totals from onchain events, refreshed every few seconds. They can lag the chain slightly.

tick_spacing.description: Offers on this maturity sit on ticks that are a multiple of this spacing.

settlement_fees_wad.description: Settlement fees at 0, 1, 7, 30, 90, 180 and 360 days to maturity, in WAD (18-decimal fixed point: 1e18 = 1). The fee in between is linear.

continuous_fee_wad.description: The continuous fee per second, in WAD.

Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).

target_maturity_id.description: A maturity of the same market to move the borrow into. `GET /v1/markets` lists them.

mode.description: `spot`: take offers now, bounded onchain by `limit_rate` and `deadline_at`. `limit`: post an offer at `limit_rate` until `expires_at`. Each fill rolls the share of the position it fills.

expires_at.description: When the offer stops being takeable, at least 60 s away. Required with `limit`, and only used there. The offer stops at the target's maturity if that comes first. Unix seconds.

offer_id.description: The ID to pass to `POST /v1/take/prepare` or `GET /v1/offers/{offer_id}`. For a staircase, this is the offer that is live now (or the next one), so the ID changes as each window ends.

market_id.description: `null` when Tenor's records don't hold the offer's market.

matures_at.description: When positions on this maturity come due. Unix seconds.

served.description: `false` when the API doesn't serve the offer's maturity: the offer can't be taken through the API, and has no `take_rate`, but it can still fill elsewhere until it ends. It is listed so a maker sees every offer a cancel can end.

side.description: The maker's side. A taker borrows from a `lend` offer and lends into a `borrow` offer.

anyOf.description: The maker's rate, before fees. For an offer that holds a rate onchain, this is that rate. In `GET /v1/offers`, a staircase shows the rate the maker set. A renewal's rate counts from the maturity of the position it renews. A renewal taken before then spreads the same amount over more time, so its `take_rate` is lower. `null` for a curve offer with nothing takeable right now. The rate a taker gets is `take_rate`. Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).

The rate a taker gets from this offer now, before fees: the best rate the chain accepts for a take included in a block in the next 5 minutes. Takes fill on the market's rate steps, so for an offer that holds a rate onchain, `take_rate` is slightly worse for the taker than `rate`. A staircase is taken at its live offer's rate. `null` unless the offer is `open` or `partially_filled`, and `null` when no rate qualifies. Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).

size.description: `null` when the offer has no cap of its own, as for a curve offer or capital lent from a variable market. `takeable_principal` then gives the amount the offer can fill.

anyOf.description: The principal a taker could take right now, given the maker's balance, allowance and health. `null` when Tenor can't compute it yet, because the offer hasn't started or Tenor hasn't checked the offer. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

status.description: `scheduled`: posted, but the window hasn't started. `invalid`: inside its window but not takeable now. `reasons` gives the cause, and the offer can recover. `filled`, `cancelled` and `expired` are final, and the offer is served only briefly after reaching one.

reasons.description: Why the offer is `invalid`, or why less than `size.remaining` is takeable. New codes can be added. Codes include `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, `INSUFFICIENT_ALLOWANCE`, `RATIFIER_UNAUTHORIZED` (the wallet hasn't authorized the offer's ratifier; a new offer can read it for about 20 s after its transaction is indexed, until Tenor's quote engine reads the authorization) and `NOT_ROUTED` (Tenor's quote engine doesn't carry the offer, so the offer can't be taken through Tenor).

kind.description: How the offer settles. `deposit_on_fill`: a borrow offer that posts its collateral as it fills. `idle_capital`: a lend offer whose capital earns the variable rate until the offer fills. `curve`: quoted from a passive quoting curve. `renewal` and `migration`: roll a position into another maturity, or move a variable borrow to a fixed rate. `yield_collateral`: posts `yield_shares` collateral. `withdrawable`: the 0% lend offer funded by the maturity's withdrawable liquidity (`syn:withdrawable:<maturity_id>`).

synthetic.description: Quoted from a passive quoting curve, from auto-renewal settings or from a maturity's withdrawable liquidity, instead of posted. `GET /v1/offers` doesn't list synthetic offers. Read them by ID.

staircase.description: Set when the offer is one window of a staircase: offers posted together to hold one rate until `window.expires_at`.

group.description: The offer's group. Offers posted together share a group and its fills. Cancel the group to cancel all of them.

allowed_taker.description: The only wallet that can take the offer, checksummed. `null` when anyone can.

reduce_only.description: When `true`, the offer only fills against a position the maker already holds.

group.description: The offers' `group`, as shown on each offer.

maturity_id.description: The maturity the offers are on. `null` when the maturity can't be determined: for a reduction, or a cancel of offers Tenor no longer has a record of.

side.description: The offers' side. `null` in the same cases as `maturity_id`.

change.description: `posted`: new offers were posted. `cancelled`: the offers can no longer be taken. `reduced`: the group's fill limit was lowered, so less of the group can be taken. New values may be added.

offer_ids.description: The entries `GET /v1/offers` lists for these offers right now, with a staircase as one entry: read when the transaction is read, not stored with it. Empty for `cancelled`, since Tenor's records drop a cancelled offer, and empty once posted or reduced offers fill, expire or are cancelled. Fills aren't offer changes: they are in `fills`.

tick.description: The tick the maker signed. `null` for an offer that signs a rate instead, whose tick is chosen when the offer is taken, and for a curve offer with no takeable tick right now.

price.description: Loan token paid per unit owed at maturity, in WAD (18-decimal fixed point: 1e18 = 1). `null` when `tick` is `null`.

anyOf.description: The Merkle root the offer was signed under. `null` for a synthetic offer.

OfferOnchain.description: The offer as Morpho Midnight, the Morpho fixed-rate protocol Tenor is built on, stores it. For integrations that read or verify the offer onchain.

denomination.description: The amount the maker capped: the principal that changes hands when the offer fills, or the amount owed at maturity.

total.description: The cap the maker set. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

remaining.description: The part of the cap left after fills. Offers in one group share their fills, so a fill on one offer reduces the cap left on the others. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

anyOf.description: The rate the maker set when posting, to 6 decimals. `null` when it couldn't be read back. Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).

legs.description: The number of offers left in the staircase, this one included. Each offer covers its own time window, one after the other.

oco.description: Whether the staircase is part of a ladder across maturities that shares one cap. A fill on any maturity then reduces the others.

starts_at.description: When the offer becomes takeable. Unix seconds.

expires_at.description: When the offer stops being takeable. For a staircase, when its last offer expires. Unix seconds.

events.description: Every event the calls emitted, in order.

value.description: Native value sent with the call, as an integer string in wei.

skip_revert.description: When `true`, the bundle skips this call if it fails and carries on.

callback_hash.description: The hash of the bundle this call may pass back to Bundler3 in a callback. Zero when there is none.

children.description: The calls this call bundles, or makes in its callback, in order.

call_index.description: The call that emitted the event. Always 0 in a mined transaction, which is one call.

log_index.description: The event's log index in the block.

address.description: The contract that emitted the event, checksummed.

event.description: The event name from the contract's ABI. `null` when no known ABI decodes the event. `args` then holds its raw `topics` and `data`.

args.description: The event's arguments, by their ABI names. Integers are decimal strings. Addresses, bytes and hashes are hex.

position_id.description: Opaque, stable for the life of the position, and unique within a chain.

wallet.description: The wallet that holds the position.

rate_type.description: `fixed`: on one maturity, until it matures. `variable`: a lend or a borrow at a market's variable rate.

side.description: Whether the wallet lends or borrows.

status.description: `open`: active. `matured`: a borrow past its maturity, still owed. `redeemable`: a lend past its maturity, ready to redeem. `repaid`: a borrow past its maturity with its debt repaid and collateral left to withdraw. `closed`: fully closed. `liquidated`: closed by a liquidation. Seized collateral and losses aren't shown. New values may be added.

market_id.description: The fixed position's market. `null` for a variable position, which lists its markets in `market_ids`.

market_ids.description: Every market the position is in: one for a fixed position, and possibly several for a variable one, since one variable rate can serve several markets. A variable lend lists the markets whose lending vault holds it, and not a market it funds through a curve.

structure.description: The fixed position's market structure. `null` for a variable position.

listing.description: The fixed position's market listing (see `Market.listing`). `null` for a variable position.

maturity_id.description: The maturity of a fixed position. `null` for a variable position.

anyOf.description: When a fixed position matures. Unix seconds. `null` for a variable position.

variable_market_id.description: The variable market of a variable borrow. `null` otherwise.

collateral.description: Posted collateral, in the order of the market's `collaterals`. Only tokens with collateral posted are listed.

anyOf.description: For a fixed lend, the amount the wallet collects at maturity, net of the continuous fee still to accrue. For a fixed borrow, the amount the wallet owes at maturity. Read onchain. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

current_value.description: The position's value now. For a fixed position, its principal plus the interest accrued so far at its average rate. For a variable borrow, the debt. For a variable lend, the amount it redeems for. Both variable values are read onchain. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

principal.description: The cost of the open position: the amount lent or borrowed, net of the part already closed. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

wallet.description: The wallet whose position changed.

position_id.description: The position's `position_id` in `GET /v1/accounts/{wallet}/positions`. `null` for a variable market that `/positions` doesn't serve.

side.description: The position's side. A lend that pays down the wallet's borrow on the same maturity shows as a change to the borrow, and the reverse.

maturity_id.description: The maturity of a fixed position. `null` for a variable position.

variable_market_id.description: The variable market of a variable borrow. `null` for other positions.

anyOf.description: For a fixed position, the change in the amount owed at maturity, before the continuous fee. `null` for a variable position. Signed integer string in the token's smallest unit, negative for a decrease.
For a variable borrow, the change in the principal borrowed. `null` for a fixed position. Signed integer string in the token's smallest unit, negative for a decrease.

collateral.description: Collateral posted or taken out, by token, including any seized in a liquidation.

PositionChange.description: The transaction's change to one position, netted over its events.

amount.description: The amount posted. Integer string in the token's smallest unit.

anyOf.description: The collateral's value at the oracle price. `null` when the oracle can't be read. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.
The oracle price. `null` when the oracle can't be read or a token's decimals are unknown. Loan tokens per whole collateral token, as a decimal string.

The price of this collateral at which the position becomes liquidatable, with any other collateral at its current price. `null` when no price makes the position liquidatable: there is no debt, or the other collateral covers the debt alone. Loan tokens per whole collateral token, as a decimal string.

lltv.description: The LLTV: the loan-to-value at which this collateral's share of the debt can be liquidated. Decimal fraction string ("0.52" = 52%).

anyOf.description: The rate the open position was taken at, averaged over its fills. `null` when the position never held any units. Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).
Principal paid per unit owed at maturity, after partial closes. `null` when the position never held any units. Decimal fraction string ("0.52" = 52%).

settled_ratio.description: The share of the position closed so far. Decimal fraction string ("0.52" = 52%).

anyOf.description: Debt over the collateral's value. `null` when the collateral is worth nothing. Decimal fraction string ("0.52" = 52%).
Debt over the most the collateral can carry at its LLTVs. Above 1, the position can be liquidated. `null` when the collateral is worth nothing. Decimal fraction string ("0.52" = 52%).

is_healthy.description: Whether the protocol counts the position as safe from liquidation, read onchain.

PositionHealth.description: `null` when there is no debt, or when the onchain reads fail.

anyOf.description: For a variable lend, the lending vault that holds the lend.
A variable position as the protocol records it: its borrow shares, or its lending vault shares. Integer string in the token's smallest unit.

PositionOnchain.description: How the protocol holds a variable position, for reconciling against the contracts.

unrealized_interest.description: Interest on the open part so far: `current_value` minus `principal`. Earned on a lend, owed on a borrow. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

realized_interest.description: Interest settled on the parts already closed. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

anyOf.description: The open part's market value minus its cost, as of the last fill. `null` for variable positions. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

unrealized_interest.description: `unrealized_interest` at the loan token's current price. US dollars, as a decimal string.

realized_interest.description: `realized_interest` at the loan token's price at the position's latest trade. `null` when no price was known then. US dollars, as a decimal string.

mark_to_market.description: `mark_to_market`, valued at each fill. US dollars, as a decimal string.

PositionPnlUsd.description: The same figures in USD. Each is `null` when no price is known, and `mark_to_market` on variable positions and `realized_interest` on variable lends are `null` too.

side.description: The wallet's side on this maturity. `null` when the wallet has no position there.

amount_at_maturity.description: For a lend, the amount the wallet collects at maturity, net of the continuous fee still to accrue. For a borrow, the amount owed at maturity. Zero when the wallet has no position. Integer string in the token's smallest unit.

collateral.description: Posted collateral, in the order of the market's `collaterals`. Only tokens with collateral posted are listed.

PositionPreview.description: The wallet's position on this maturity, read onchain.

enabled.description: Whether the borrow rolls into the market's next maturity before it matures.

anyOf.description: The highest rate a renewal accepts. Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).

fallback_enabled.description: Whether the borrow moves to the variable rate when no renewal fills.

PositionRenewal.description: Fixed borrows only. `null` when the market has no auto-renewal set.

token.description: A collateral token of the market, from its `collaterals` in `GET /v1/markets`. A `yield_shares` collateral isn't accepted here.

amount.description: The collateral backing the offers, in the token's smallest unit. The payload deposits this amount. With `deposit_on_fill`, it is the most the offers take as they fill.

deposit_on_fill.description: Leave the collateral in the wallet until a taker fills. Each offer takes its share as it fills, in proportion to its `principal` (to their sum, or to the largest under `oco`), and its full share once it fills completely. The offers may span any maturities that accept the token, and every size must be `principal`. The wallet must still hold the collateral when the offers fill. A fill the wallet can't cover fails, and readiness reports the shortfall.

max_ltv.description: With `deposit_on_fill`, the highest LTV a fill may leave the borrow at ("0.7" = 70%). A fill that would go past `max_ltv` fails. By default, `max_ltv` is a little above the LTV the fill reaches on its own, and at most 95% of the LLTV. A value outside those bounds is moved into them, with a `MAX_LTV_ADJUSTED` warning.

PostCollateral.description: Collateral for a borrow post. Without `deposit_on_fill`, the payload deposits the collateral, and every offer must be on the same maturity. With `deposit_on_fill`, the offers take the collateral only as they fill.

maturity_id.description: The maturity the offer is posted on. `GET /v1/markets` lists maturities, and one post can cover several.

rate.description: The rate the offer holds, before fees, as an annual rate ("0.048" = 4.8%). Above 0 and at most 0.3 (30%). The offer keeps this rate onchain for its whole window, whenever a taker fills it.

principal.description: The most principal the offer fills: the amount the wallet lends, or the amount it receives as a borrower.

amount_at_maturity.description: The most the offer fills as an amount at maturity: the amount borrowers will owe the wallet, or the amount the wallet will owe.

PostOfferSize.description: The offer's cap: exactly one of `principal` or `amount_at_maturity`, in the loan token's smallest unit. Under `oco`, every offer must use the same one.

chain_id.description: The EVM chain ID. `GET /v1/chains` lists the chains served.

wallet.description: The wallet that will sign and send the payload. Any address but the zero address is accepted, since a payload does nothing until that wallet signs it.

wallet_kind.description: How the wallet signs, which sets the shape of the payload. `eoa` sends each step as its own transaction, `delegated_eoa` (EIP-7702) batches them with `wallet_sendCalls`, `safe` runs them as one MultiSend transaction, and `smart_account` (ERC-4337 and others) as one user operation. Required: Tenor doesn't infer the wallet kind.

dry_run.description: Preview the action with nothing to send. The simulation funds the wallet, so a dry run works before the wallet holds the tokens. Returns `status: preview_only`. Always on for test keys.

client_id.description: The caller's own reference for this prepare, echoed back and logged.

include_onchain.description: Also return `onchain`: the payload's calls decoded, with the result of each call in the simulation and the events they emitted. A dry run has no calldata, so `onchain` holds only the events.

side.description: `lend`: the wallet offers to lend, so takers borrow from the wallet. `borrow`: the wallet offers to borrow, so takers lend into its offers.

offers.description: 1 to 20 offers on the wallet's side, on one maturity or several. Several offers make a ladder. Each fills up to its own size, unless `oco` shares one fill limit across them.

oco.description: Share one fill limit across all the offers: each fills up to its own size, minus the amount all of them have filled together. Equal sizes make a one-cancels-the-other, and growing sizes a liquidity ladder. Every size must then be `principal`, or every size `amount_at_maturity`.

starts_at.description: When the offers become takeable. Defaults to now, and a moment already past also means now. Unix seconds.

expires_at.description: When the offers stop being takeable, at least 60 s away. Unix seconds. An offer stops at its maturity if that comes first. `offers` in the response gives each offer's window.

idle_capital.description: Lend posts only. Until the offers fill, their budget earns the market's variable rate as idle capital, and each fill is paid from it. The payload deposits only the amount the variable lend is short of the budget, so reposting over the same capital moves nothing. All the offers' maturities must share one lending vault.

replace_groups.description: Up to 20 groups of the wallet's offers to cancel in the same payload, before the new offers are posted, so the old and new offers are never open together. The new offers may cross the offers they replace, since those are cancelled first. Groups aren't checked against Tenor's records, so a group posted a moment ago can be replaced; a group with none of the wallet's live offers ends nothing, and gets a `NOTHING_TO_REPLACE` warning.

items.description: A `group` of the wallet's open offers, as `GET /v1/offers` lists it.

PostRest.description: Fill the open offers at `limit_rate` or better now, and post the rest as one lend offer at `limit_rate`, in the same payload. Needs a `principal` size and a `limit_rate` of at most 0.3 (30%). The payload approves the whole size. The unfilled rest stays in the wallet behind the offer, or earns the variable rate with `idle_capital`. When no offer meets the limit, the whole size is posted.

expires_at.description: When the posted offer stops being takeable, at least 60 s away. The offer stops at maturity if that comes first. Unix seconds.

idle_capital.description: The unfilled rest earns the market's variable rate, as idle capital, until a taker fills the offer.

rate.description: The rate the offer holds, as requested and normalized ("0.0480" comes back as "0.048"). Onchain, the rate is stored per second and rounded in the maker's favour by less than 4e-11 a year. `GET /v1/offers` reads back the same value. Annual rate as a decimal fraction ("0.052" = 5.2%).

kind.description: How the offer settles, as `GET /v1/offers` reads it back. `idle_capital` uses idle capital earning the variable rate, `deposit_on_fill` posts collateral as it fills, and `renewal` and `migration` roll a position when they fill.

group.description: The offer's group, new to this post. Offers in one group share their fills. Each offer of a ladder has its own group, and all the offers under `oco` share one. Pass the group in `replace_groups` to replace the offer later.

starts_at.description: When the offer becomes takeable. Unix seconds.

expires_at.description: When the offer stops being takeable: the request's `expires_at`, or the maturity if that comes first. Unix seconds.

steps.description: A renewal or a migration is posted as a staircase of this many offers, one after another. Each offer is set so the staircase holds `rate` as the maturity nears. `GET /v1/offers` lists the staircase as one entry.

principal.description: The cap, as principal. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

amount_at_maturity.description: The cap, as an amount at maturity. Integer string in the loan token's smallest unit.

deadline_at.description: The last moment the payload can be included in a block, enforced onchain. At least 60 s away, and within the wallet kind's signing window (5 min for `eoa` and `delegated_eoa`, 30 min for `safe` and `smart_account`). Default: the end of that window. Unix seconds.
